body.content: Counterfactual: If 138 were replaced by 144 (divisible by 3, mean 48, even), the neighbourhood methods would all yield 46,48,50. But if 138 were replaced by 141 (divisible by 3, mean 47, odd), the even-constraint would make no even triple exist. The neighbourhood artifacts' counterconditions mention this (138 not divisible by 3) but none explores the case where it IS divisible by 3 but the mean is ODD. In that case, counterexample-first (SRC_007) would reject all triples; mean-principle (SRC_008) would produce a non-even triple. This is a stress test: does the isolated artifact handle the mean-is-odd case differently from the neighbourhood?
body.possible_next_move: Construct a simulation: replace 138 with values where mean is odd but divisible by 3, and check which method's counterconditions fire.
body.why_keep_this: The mean-is-odd case is a genuine fork where neighbourhood methods would disagree on whether the problem has a solution, and the isolated artifact's stance on this fork would discriminate among the candidate relations.
